title: Complementation of Lymphotoxin α Knockout Mice with Tumor Necrosis Factor–expressing Transgenes Rectifies Defective Splenic Structure and Function
authors: Lena Alexopoulou; Manolis Pasparakis; George Kollias
id: Matched: Measurement of TNF Production after LPS Stimulation.
abstract: LTα knockout mice were complemented with TNF-expressing transgenes to study splenic structure and function. This restored B/T cell zone segregation and partially preserved B cell follicles, FDC networks, and germinal centers.

title: Antagonism of the histamine H4 receptor reduces LPS-induced TNF production in vivo
authors: Jeffery M. Cowden; Fuqu Yu; Mamatha Challapalli; Jing-Feng Huang; Sunhwa Kim; Wai-Ping Fung-Leung; J...
abstract: Histamine H4 receptor antagonists and deficiency reduced LPS-induced TNF production in mice. This suggests H4 receptor activation contributes to TLR-mediated inflammation in vivo, particularly in the liver.

title: Transmembrane TNFα-Expressed Macrophage Membrane-Coated Chitosan Nanoparticles as Cancer Therapeutics
authors: Srirupa Bhattacharyya; Siddhartha Sankar Ghosh
abstract: Macrophage membranes expressing TNFα were used to coat chitosan nanoparticles. These nanoparticles showed significant anti-cancer effects and good biocompatibility.

title: Macrophage priming and lipopolysaccharide-triggered release of tumor necrosis factor alpha during graft-versus-host disease
abstract: This study examined macrophage activation and TNF-alpha release during graft-versus-host disease (GVHD). Macrophages are primed during GVHD, leading to lethal TNF-alpha release upon encountering endogenous lipopolysaccharide.

title: Lipopolysaccharide-induced selective priming effects on tumor necrosis factor alpha and nitric oxide production in mouse peritoneal macrophages
abstract: Macrophages were precultured with low-dose LPS, then restimulated. This pretreatment selectively primes macrophages for differential responses to subsequent stimuli, rather than causing total refractoriness.

title: Extinction of the tumor necrosis factor locus, and of genes encoding the lipopolysaccharide signaling pathway
abstract: The TNF gene and LPS signaling pathway were studied in macrophage-fibroblast hybrids. Fusion activated a system that silenced TNF and LPS signaling, potentially during cell differentiation.

title: LPS‐stimulated NF‐κB p65 dynamic response marks the initiation of TNF expression and transition to IL‐10 expression in RAW 264.7 macrophages
authors: Stuart Hobbs; Marinaliz Reynoso; Alyssa V. Geddis; Alexander Y. Mitrophanov; Ronald W. Matheny
id: Matched: LPS stimulation of IL‐10 expression occurs subsequent to TNFα expressi
abstract: LPS stimulation kinetics of NF-κB, TNF-α, and IL-10 were studied in macrophages. NF-κB activation precedes TNF-α expression, which then transitions to IL-10 expression.

authors: S. Dey, D. Boucher, J. W. Pitchford, D. Lagos *
id: Matched: Macrophage community AIH is dependent on LPS dose
abstract: This study mathematically models macrophage responses to LPS, analyzing single-cell protein expression. Macrophage hypo-responsiveness to secondary LPS challenges is driven by altered transition rates to non-responsive states.

authors: Ping Li; Yonghong Wu; Manxiang Li; Xiaojuan Qiu; Xiaoyan Bai; Xiaojing Zhao

abstract: AS-703026 was studied for its effect on LPS-induced TNFα production in macrophages and human cells. The compound inhibits TNFα production through MEK/ERK dependent and independent pathways, including NFκB inhibition.

title: Lipopolysaccharide regulation of antiinflammatory tristetraprolin family and proinflammatory gene expression in mouse macrophages
authors: Heping Cao
id: Matched: Effect of LPS on proinflammatory gene expression
abstract: Lipopolysaccharide (LPS) was studied for its effects on tristetraprolin (TTP) family and proinflammatory gene expression in mouse macrophages. LPS increased TTP, TNF, and COX2 mRNA but had minimal impact on other TTP homologues and proinflammatory cytokine genes.

title: Augmentation and Suppression of Release of Tumor Necrosis Factor from Macrophages by Negatively Charged Phospholipids
authors: Satoru Yui; Masatoshi Yamazaki
abstract: Negatively charged phospholipids, cardiolipin and peroxidized phosphatidylserine, were studied for their effects on macrophage TNF release. High concentrations of these lipids suppressed TNF release, while lower concentrations augmented it.

title: Macrophage tumor necrosis factor-alpha deletion does not protect against obesity-associated metabolic dysfunction

id: Matched: TNF-αF/F,LyzMCre mice display significantly reduced circulating TNF-α
abstract: Macrophage TNF-α deletion was studied in mice on a high-fat diet. This deletion did not prevent obesity or associated metabolic dysfunction.

title: Kappa B-type enhancers are involved in lipopolysaccharide-mediated transcriptional activation of the tumor necrosis factor alpha gene in primary macrophages
authors: Matched: cat /papers/PMC2187654/content.lines --lines 5
abstract: Kappa B-type enhancers were studied for their role in LPS-mediated TNF-alpha gene activation in macrophages. These enhancers, along with factors interacting with the Y box, are crucial for LPS-induced TNF-alpha gene transcription.

title: Macrophages employ quorum licensing to regulate collective activation
authors: Joseph J. Muldoon; Yishan Chuang; Neda Bagheri; Joshua N. Leonard
id: Matched: TNF expression is heterogeneous and varies with cell density
abstract: Macrophages exhibit bimodal activation states influenced by cell density and prior signaling history, not just LPS. This "quorum licensing" mechanism non-linearly couples density to collective TNF production, potentially amplifying responses to threats.

title: Mathematical modelling of activation-induced heterogeneity in TNF, IL6, NOS2, and IL1β expression reveals cell state transitions underpinning macrophage responses to LPS
authors: Shoumit Dey; Dave Boucher; Jon Pitchford; Dimitris Lagos
id: Matched: Macrophage community AIH is dependent on LPS dose
abstract: Mathematical models explored macrophage states and their responses to LPS. Macrophage hypo-responsiveness to a second LPS challenge is driven by altered transition rates between activation states.

title: Divergent effects of tumor necrosis factor (TNF) in sepsis: a meta-analysis of experimental studies
authors: Christian Kassasseya; Ligia Iulia Torsin; Caroline Musset; Marc Benhamou; Irshad H. Chaudry; Jean-Ma...
abstract: This meta-analysis examined experimental studies on TNF's role in sepsis. TNF inactivation and LPS models showed detrimental effects, while TNF injection and live bacterial models demonstrated adaptive roles.

title: Signaling pathways involved in LPS induced TNFalpha production in human adipocytes
authors: Laurence Hoareau; Karima Bencharif; Philippe Rondeau; Ravi Murumalla; Palaniyandi Ravanan; Frank Tal...
id: Matched: Macrophages are more sensitive to LPS, but adipocytes secrete more TNF
abstract: Human adipocytes were treated with LPS to study TNFalpha production. TNFalpha secretion is primarily mediated by NFkappaB and p38 MAP Kinase pathways, with PI3Kinase involved in the initial step.

title: Differential Cell Sensitivity between OTA and LPS upon Releasing TNF-α
authors: Lauy Al-Anati; Ebtisam Essid; Ulla Stenius; Knut Beuerlein; Klaus Schuh; Ernst Petzinger

abstract: This study compared TNF-α release from various cell lines exposed to ochratoxin A (OTA) and lipopolysaccharide (LPS). Macrophages and macrophage-derived cells, but not other cell types, released TNF-α in response to OTA.

title: RNA from LPS-stirnulated macrophages induces the release of tumour necrosis factor-α and interleukin-1 by resident macrophages
authors: R. A. Ribeiro, F. L. De Lucca, C. A. Flores, F. Q. Cunha, S. H. Ferreira

authors: Kinga Borzęcka; Agnieszka Płóciennikowska; Hanna Björkelund; Andrzej Sobota; Katarzyna Kwiatkowska
abstract: CD14's role in LPS binding and TNF-α production was analyzed. CD14 is crucial for low-dose LPS binding and TNF-α production, but its role diminishes at higher LPS doses.

title: Lead Increases Lipopolysaccharide-Induced Liver Injury through Tumor Necrosis Factor-α Overexpression by Monocytes/Macrophages: Role of Protein Kinase C and p42/44 Mitogen-Activated Protein Kinase
authors: Yu-Jung Cheng; Bei-Chang Yang; Ming-Yie Liu
abstract: Lead exposure amplifies lipopolysaccharide-induced liver injury by increasing TNF-α production in monocytes/macrophages. This occurs via the PKC/MAPK pathway, leading to excessive TNF-α and subsequent liver damage.

title: Tumor Necrosis Factor (TNF) Receptor Shedding Controls Thresholds of Innate Immune Activation That Balance Opposing TNF Functions in Infectious and Inflammatory Diseases
authors: Sofia Xanthoulea; Manolis Pasparakis; Stavroula Kousteni; Cord Brakebusch; David Wallach; Jan Bauer;...
id: Matched: TNF and LPS Administration and Listeria Infection.
abstract: This study investigated the role of p55TNF receptor shedding in regulating innate immune responses. Blocking receptor shedding leads to hyperactive immunity, improving infection control but increasing susceptibility to inflammatory diseases.

abstract: Ipratropium and tiotropium were studied for their anti-inflammatory effects in macrophage models. These drugs were found to reduce pro-inflammatory cytokines, though less effectively than budesonide and fenoterol.

title: Catecholamines Attenuate LPS-Induced Inflammation through β2 Adrenergic Receptor Activation- and PKA Phosphorylation-Mediated TLR4 Downregulation in Macrophages
authors: Cong Wang; Guo-Gang Feng; Junko Takagi; Yoshihiro Fujiwara; Tsuyoshi Sano; Hideaki Note
id: Matched: 3.1. LPS Induced TNFα Expression in RAW264.7 Cells
abstract: Catecholamines were studied for their anti-inflammatory effects on LPS-induced inflammation in macrophages. Catecholamines suppress inflammation by activating β2-AR, leading to PKA-mediated TLR4 downregulation.

title: Apigenin-7-Glucuronide from Urera aurantiaca Inhibits Tumor Necrosis Factor Alpha and Total Nitrite Release in Lipopolysaccharide-Activated Macrophages
authors: Carla Marrassini; Laura Cogoi; Valeria Sülsen; Claudia Anesini
abstract: Apigenin-7-glucuronide (A7G) was isolated from *Urera aurantiaca* and its anti-inflammatory effects were studied. A7G significantly inhibited TNF-α and total nitrite release in activated macrophages, validating the plant's traditional use.

title: Induction of Tumor Necrosis Factor in Mice by Recombinant Human Macrophage Colony‐stimulating Factor
authors: Takuma Sakurai, Shinya Suzu, Muneo Yamada, Nobuya Yanai, Takuji Kawashima, Kiyohiko Hatake, Fumimaro...
abstract: Recombinant human macrophage colony-stimulating factor (rhM-CSF) was studied for its effect on TNF production in mice. rhM-CSF primes mice for LPS-induced TNF production, suggesting potential in cancer immunotherapy.

authors: Ning Li; Samuel Katz; Bhaskar Dutta; Zachary L. Benet; Jing Sun; Iain D.C. Fraser
id: Matched: Day 4: TNF-α reporter imaging data collection
abstract: A genome-wide siRNA screen identified genes regulating LPS-induced NF-κB and TNF-α responses in mouse macrophages. This study provides a resource for analyzing gene function in this key inflammatory pathway.

title: TNF Tolerance in Monocytes and Macrophages: Characteristics and Molecular Mechanisms
authors: René Huber; Rolf Bikker; Bastian Welz; Martin Christmann; Korbinian Brand
abstract: This review examines TNF tolerance in monocytes and macrophages, detailing its characteristics and molecular mechanisms. TNF tolerance can terminate inflammation or cause immune paralysis, with potential diagnostic and therapeutic implications.

title: Vitamin C Mitigates Oxidative Stress and Tumor Necrosis Factor-Alpha in Severe Community-Acquired Pneumonia and LPS-Induced Macrophages
authors: Yuanyuan Chen; Guangyan Luo; Jiao Yuan; Yuanyuan Wang; Xiaoqiong Yang; Xiaoyun Wang; Guoping Li; Zhi...
id: Matched: 3.5. Vitamin C Inhibited LPS-Induced ROS, TNF-α, and P38 in MH-S Cell
abstract: Severe community-acquired pneumonia patients showed increased oxidative stress and inflammation. Vitamin C treatment reduced these markers, suggesting a therapeutic role in severe CAP.

title: Genome-wide siRNA screen of genes regulating the LPS-induced TNF-α response in human macrophages
authors: Jing Sun; Samuel Katz; Bhaskar Dutta; Ze Wang; Iain D.C. Fraser
abstract: A genome-wide siRNA screen identified genes regulating the LPS-induced TNF-α response in human macrophages. Novel hits broadly affect innate inflammatory responses to microbial stimuli.

title: Inhibiting TNF-α signaling does not attenuate induction of endotoxin tolerance
authors: Christopher Loosbroock; Kenneth W Hunter
abstract: This study investigated if inhibiting TNF-α signaling affects endotoxin tolerance induction. Blocking TNF-α signaling reduced inflammatory cytokine production but did not prevent endotoxin tolerance.

authors: Taha Salim; Cheryl L. Sershen; Elebeoba E. May
abstract: A mathematical model simulated iNOS gene expression in LPS-stimulated macrophages. IFN-γ priming is essential for robust iNOS expression and NO production, while TNF-α primarily affects response speed.

abstract: PTPN7's role in regulating TNF-α production in LPS-stimulated macrophages was studied. PTPN7 negatively regulates TNF-α expression and the inflammatory response by inactivating ERK1/2 and p38 MAPKs.

title: Upregulating Nonneuronal Cholinergic Activity Decreases TNF Release from Lipopolysaccharide-Stimulated RAW264.7 Cells
authors: Yi Lv; Sen Hu; Jiangyang Lu; Ning Dong; Qian Liu; Minghua Du; Huiping Zhang
id: Matched: 3.1. LPS Stimulation Induces the Enhancement of Both TNF Release and m
abstract: LPS stimulation was found to modulate nonneuronal cholinergic activity in RAW264.7 cells. Enhancing autocrine ACh production can reduce TNF release from these cells.

authors: Richard Haworth; Nick Platt; Satish Keshav; Derralynn Hughes; Elisabeth Darley; Hiroshi Suzuki; Yuki...

abstract: Activated macrophages express scavenger receptor A (SR-A), which protects against lethal endotoxic shock. SR-A limits LPS-induced cytokine release and scavenges LPS, reducing mortality.

authors: Jiro Sakai, Eugenia Cammarota, John A. Wright, Pietro Cicuta, Rachel A. Gottschalk, Ning Li, Iain D....
abstract: This study investigated LPS-induced NF-κB nuclear translocation and TNFα expression in macrophages. MyD88 is the primary driver of NF-κB translocation, while both MyD88 and TRIF are required for TNFα expression.

authors: P Myrianthefs; K Venetsanou; E Grouzi; E Boutzouka; P Evagelopoulou; G Fildissis; I Spiliotopoulou; ...

abstract: Estrogen rapidly inhibits lipopolysaccharide-induced TNF-α production in macrophages. This occurs via GPR30-mediated calcium influx, which suppresses p38 MAPK activation.

title: Pre-Treatment of Recombinant Mouse MFG-E8 Downregulates LPS-Induced TNF-α Production in Macrophages via STAT3-Mediated SOCS3 Activation
authors: Monowar Aziz; Asha Jacob; Akihisa Matsuda; Rongqian Wu; Mian Zhou; Weifeng Dong; Weng-Lang Yang; Pin...
abstract: Recombinant mouse MFG-E8 was studied for its effect on LPS-induced TNF-α production in macrophages. Pre-treatment with MFG-E8 downregulated TNF-α by activating STAT3-mediated SOCS3, which negatively regulates TLR4 signaling.

title: LITAF Mediation of Increased TNF-α Secretion from Inflamed Colonic Lamina Propria Macrophages

abstract: This study investigated LITAF's role in TNF-α secretion from inflamed colonic macrophages. LITAF mediates increased TNF-α production in these cells during acute inflammation.

title: Modulation of Tumor Necrosis Factor by Microbial Pathogens
authors: Masmudur M Rahman; Grant McFadden
abstract: This paper reviews how microbial pathogens, like viruses and bacteria, manipulate the host's tumor necrosis factor (TNF) response. Pathogens employ diverse strategies to block or alter TNF signaling, offering insights into disease and potential therapeutic targets.

title: Unaltered TNF-α production by macrophages and monocytes in diet-induced obesity in the rat
authors: Sammy Bedoui; Elena Velkoska; Steve Bozinovski; Jessica E Jones; Gary P Anderson; Margaret J Morris
abstract: This study investigated TNF-α production by monocytes and macrophages in diet-induced obese rats. No significant differences in TNF-α production were found between obese and control rats, suggesting dietary obesity does not mimic immune defects seen in genetically obese models.

title: Globular Adiponectin Causes Tolerance to LPS-Induced TNF-α Expression via Autophagy Induction in RAW 264.7 Macrophages: Involvement of SIRT1/FoxO3A Axis
authors: Nirmala Tilija Pun; Amit Subedi; Mi Jin Kim; Pil-Hoon Park
abstract: Globular adiponectin was studied for its role in suppressing LPS-induced TNF-α expression in macrophages. Autophagy induction, mediated by the SIRT1/FoxO3A axis, is identified as a key mechanism for this suppression.

title: Lipopolysaccharide and Tumor Necrosis Factor Regulate Parkin Expression via Nuclear Factor-Kappa B
authors: Thi A. Tran; Andrew D. Nguyen; Jianjun Chang; Matthew S. Goldberg; Jae-Kyung Lee; Malú G. Tansey

authors: Heyuan Liu; Lixia Kai; Huahua Du; Xinxia Wang; Yizhen Wang
abstract: LPS was studied for its effect on intestinal fatty acid absorption. Macrophage-secreted TNF-α, induced by LPS, inhibits fatty acid absorption in enterocytes via caspase-3 activation.

title: Intracellular NAD+ levels are associated with LPS-induced TNF-α release in pro-inflammatory macrophages
authors: Abbas Jawad Al-Shabany; Alan John Moody; Andrew David Foey; Richard Andrew Billington
abstract: Intracellular NAD+ levels were studied in pro-inflammatory and anti-inflammatory macrophages stimulated with lipopolysaccharide. NAD+ levels in pro-inflammatory macrophages correlated with TNF-α release.

authors: Joseph Skurski; Garima Dixit; Carl P. Blobel; Priya D. Issuree; Thorsten Maretzky
abstract: This study investigated how lipopolysaccharide (LPS) dose affects inflammatory responses in macrophages, focusing on the role of iRhom2. Low LPS doses trigger a sustained inflammatory loop dependent on iRhom2/ADAM17 and TNF receptor signaling, which is absent at high doses.

authors: Yufeng Lou; Zhenrong Huang

abstract: This study investigated miR-15a-5p's role in macrophage inflammation during sepsis. miR-15a-5p targets TNIP2, reducing inflammatory cytokine secretion and NF-κ pathway activation.
